scenarios.expected: Each claimed configuration path is demonstrated with actual requests/files and recorded effective values excluding secrets. Wrong origin, limits, unavailable storage/engine, and mismatched encryption keys fail as documented and recover after correction.
scenarios.actual: Exercised each configuration path on the same disposable installation with actual requests and files. Storage: wrote a Document on the local driver, switched to a local S3-compatible store and then to an Azure Blob emulator, and after each switch downloaded every file written under every earlier driver with matching SHA-256 values, with worker processing checked on each driver. Limits: MAX_UPLOAD_MB=1 refused a 1,100,000-byte upload with HTTP 413 and "That file is over the 1 MB upload limit." while a smaller file was stored and downloaded byte-identical. Engine bounds: DOC_ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS=900000 stopped app and worker startup with the message naming the 420000 maximum, and removing it recovered readiness. Proxy: a local Caddy instance with its internal CA served https://openlaw-review.localhost:43372, and sign-in, an upload and download, an unbuffered /api/events stream and an invitation carrying that origin all worked through it, while a sign-in posted with a foreign Origin was refused. Database: an external DATABASE_URL migrated a separate empty Postgres 16 service, took its own Administrator and Contract, and removing the setting returned the original bundled database with its records and files intact. Email and keys: the saved relay delivered, an environment SMTP_URL override took precedence and failed delivery, removing it restored the saved relay, and a key rotation with OPENLAW_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS re-encrypted the stored credential ("Stored credentials resealed under the key in use: smtp_url (1)") with real delivery before and after retiring the old key. A wrong key left records readable but the saved relay unusable, and the retained key restored delivery. No secret was printed into this evidence.

limitations: S3 and Azure Blob were exercised against owned local compatible services with explicit disposable keys; no cloud identity credential chain was tested.
The HTTPS origin used a local Caddy internal CA accepted only by the reviewer's browser context.
Local TLS uses an isolated Caddy internal CA and does not certify public DNS or certificate issuance.
S3 and Azure operations use owned local compatible services and explicit disposable keys; no cloud identity credential-chain claim.
Provider guides remain on unmerged PR #783; real provider checks C42/C43 are still blocked and are not waived.
The user will proofread the assembled complete suite; no human proofreading or feature-owner sign-off is recorded.

technicalReview.scope: Read the release under test for the behaviour the operator guides claim: the credential-key floor and the absence of one on AUTH_SECRET (packages/db/src/secrets.ts, apps/api/src/index.ts, apps/worker/src/index.ts), the doc-engine bounds and their boot-time refusal (apps/api/src/lib/doc-engine/config.ts, apps/api/src/lib/doc-engine/http.ts), the upload ceiling's silent fallback (apps/api/src/lib/uploads.ts), where outbound email is resolved and tested (apps/api/src/modules/email-settings/routes.ts), the event stream's frames and headers (apps/api/src/modules/events/routes.ts), the journal guard and its messages (packages/db/src/migration-journal.ts), the two refusals of 0060_account_issuer (packages/db/migrations/0060_account_issuer.sql), and the deployment topology and defaults (compose.yml, Dockerfile, .env.example, docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). This reading produced the five corrections in the first review commit. It is recorded separately from the container-operation walkthroughs and does not close a scenario on its own.
